title: Token timeline synthesis and cache-reconciliation instrumentation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We need an instrumentation strategy that synthesizes a per-token timeline from heterogeneous traces (runtime spans, ingress/egress, batching gates) and reconciles that timeline with KV cache hits/misses to produce accurate token-level latency and cost attribution. Current telemetry shows token-level spikes but lacks a consistent mapping between low-level spans and the logical token positions for batched and streamed requests, leading to over/under-counting of GPU token time in dashboards and billing reconciliations.
acceptance_criteria: Produce a token timeline model that maps each emitted token to a sequence of spans and KV-cache events with a probabilistic confidence score.
Integrate a cache-reconciliation stage that attributes negative delta (cache speedup) vs positive delta (cache miss cost) per-token and surface both as separate metrics.
Dashboards updated: per-request token latency heatmap, per-token cache-impact waterfall, and an aggregated billing-accurate token-cost KPI.
Backfill last 14 days of telemetry for selected customers using the new reconciliation algorithm with error bounds logged.
Unit + integration tests for span-stitching logic and the pipeline transformation.
implementation_notes: Plan: 1) Define canonical token timeline proto used by runtime and tracing libs (lightweight fields: request_id, token_index, timestamp_ms, span_refs[], cache_event_id). 2) Extend runtime to emit token-boundary markers at the batch frontier and streaming flush points. 3) Enrich trace collector to accept token markers and KV-cache events and perform a windowed join to synthesize token timelines. 4) Run an offline reconciliation job that computes per-token cost deltas and writes both raw and synthesized metrics to the metrics pipeline (Prometheus-compatible labels + LTS logs). 5) Expose results in Console: graph, heatmap, and per-request drilldown. Implementation will use existing tracing hook RFC and add a new ingestion microservice 'token-reconciler'.
updates: 2025-11-14: Ticket created after on-call review flagged discrepancies in per-token cost numbers for burst workloads.
2025-11-21: Spiked prototype for token markers in a dev runtime build; identified race with streaming flush that requires a deterministic flush marker.
2025-11-24: Design review with runtime and tracing teams — agreed on minimal token marker payload to avoid p99 inflation.
2025-11-28: Data engineering scoped an offline join job using Spark for backfill; plan to move to Flink for streaming reconciliation.
2025-12-02: Implemented collector-side windowed join; initial unit tests pass; failing an edge-case where batch coalesce hides token_index order — investigating.
risks: Runtime instrumentation could add non-trivial overhead at high QPS if token markers are too chatty.
Batch reordering at the proxy layer may obscure token_index ordering; may need sequence stamping at ingress.
Backfill cost for 14 days of high-volume telemetry is significant — require throttling and sampling strategies.
Edge cases with partial KV cache state (warm-start) could bias early tokens; need to surface confidence scores.
qa_plan: Run integration tests in staging with synthetic workloads: (a) single-request stream, (b) large batch with mixed cache hits/misses, (c) interleaved streaming + batching. Verify synthesized timelines against tracer logs and GPU utilization traces. Run backfill on a 1% sample of production tenants and compare aggregated token-cost KPI to previous baseline within +-5% or explainable delta.
